name_note: GTDB R232 g__Enterobacter also contains a minority of genomes labelled Escherichia or Leclercia in NCBI, so it is slightly broader than the classical genus.

sentences.text: A systematic review of ESKAPE pathogens in Africa, a group that includes Enterobacter spp., found stool samples had the highest pooled prevalence, followed by urine, nasal and blood samples.
That same review estimated a pooled prevalence of 20% for Enterobacter spp. among the ESKAPE pathogens it covered.
A study of 67 infants reported that stool collected at birth, six weeks and fourteen weeks yielded Enterobacter species alongside Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
